the pro-segments of cysteine and serine proteases play an important role in their activation mechanism by regulating their folding and activity.

the zymogen pro-segment of papain undergoes a rearrangements at low pH which triggers its autocatalytic proteolytic activation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanism of the activation of papain and its thermostable mutant.
the molecular mechanism of activation of the zymogens of cysteine proteinases and the factors responsible for their higher thermal stability.
understanding the structural and molecular mechanisms of the regulation of proteolytical activity of papain-like enzymes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structure of the pro-segment in the zymogenic state of papain is the major determinant of the latency of its activity.

the structure of the zzymogen of the papain-like cysteine protease is maintained in the form of an inactive state at neutral pH by its pro-segments, which undergoes a conformational rearrangement to a more relaxed structure at acidic pH to trigger the autocatalytic activation cascade.
the structure of the zyme of papain reveals its activation process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the structure of the zyme of the thermostable mutant has provided an explanation for the maintenance of latency in the zymogens of cysteine and serine proteases, which have been considered to be a mystery for decades.
the pro-segments of cysteine and aspartyl proteases have a common mechanism for maintaining latency of the protease activity in the zymogens.
the pro-segments in the clan C1A proteases play a key role in the activation of these enzymes and that their removal leads to the activation of the protease.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the pro-segments of the zymogens of cysteine and serine proteases are not merely a structural scaffold for the correct folding of the zymogenic proteases, but also act as a molecular timer to maintain latency at neutral pH and as a molecular trigger for the autocatalytic activation at acidic pH.
the pro-segments of the cysteine protease family are not merely structural elements, as previously believed.
the pro-segments of cysteine proteinases are not merely a scaffold that is removed after proteolytic activation but rather are a part of the activation mechanism.
